Our results indicate that there is no elevation of cTn despite the occurrence of significant WMAs on DSE. We conclude that cTnI cannot be used as an additional diagnostic tool during pharmacological stress test performed to evaluate the presence and severity of ischemia.

In simpler terms, dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE) is a test that uses medication to simulate heart attacks in patients. The results of this test showed no increase in cardiac troponin levels even when significant wall motion abnormalities (WMAs) were present on the echocardiogram. This suggests that cTnI, which measures the level of cardiac muscle damage, may not be a reliable indicator of ischemia or heart attack severity during DSE testing.

However, it's essential to note that this does not necessarily mean that dobutamine stress echocardiography is ineffective in diagnosing coronary artery disease or assessing patient risk for heart attacks. Other tests and assessments, such as electrocardiograms (ECGs) and other imaging modalities, may be necessary to fully evaluate a patient's cardiac health.
